p.seg: Miscellaneous Matters, Section One
In the past, Shùn personally engaged in farming, pottery, and fishing, while embodying filial piety and brotherly love.
His father, Gǔsǒu, was stubborn,
his mother was ignorant, and his younger brother, Xiàng, was arrogant.
All were incorrigibly foolish.
Shùn exhausted the way of filial piety
in order to support Gǔsǒu.
Gǔsǒu and Xiàng plotted to dig a well and plaster a granary,
intending to kill Shùn.
Shùn’s filial piety became even more earnest.
When going to the fields, he would wail and weep.
At fifty years old,
he still yearned like an infant.
He can be called the epitome of filial piety.
Therefore, when he farmed at Mount Lì,
the farmers of Mount Lì yielded the boundaries of their fields;
when he made pottery on the banks of the Hé River,
the potters of the Hé River
did not make inferior vessels;
when he fished at Léizé Lake,
the fishermen of Léizé shared their catch equally.
And when he became the Son of Heaven,
the world was transformed by him.
The barbarian tribes all submitted.
To the north, he reached Qú Sōu,
He pacified Jiāozhǐ in the south,
and none did not admire righteousness,
with unicorns and phoenixes in the suburbs.
Therefore, Confucius said:
"The utmost in filial piety and fraternal love
penetrates to the spirits and gods,
and shines upon the four seas."
This speaks of Shùn.
Confucius was in his district and village,
earnestly practicing filial piety,
and residing in Quēdǎng.
The children of Quēdǎng farmed and fished,
and when dividing the catch, those with parents received more,
because he transformed them through filial piety.
Therefore, seventy-two disciples came from afar,
submitting to his virtue.
In Lǔ, there was a man named Shěn Yóushì,
who fed his sheep until they were full in the morning,
in order to deceive the market people.
Gōng Shènshì had a wife who was promiscuous.
Shèn Kuìshì was extravagant, arrogant, and dissolute.
Those in the Lǔ market who sold cattle and horses were skilled at pre-bargaining.
When Confucius was about to become the Minister of Justice of Lǔ,
Shěn Yóushì dared not feed his sheep in the morning,
Gōng Shènshì divorced his wife,
Shèn Kuìshì crossed the border and moved away,
those in Lǔ who sold horses and cattle did not pre-bargain,
but displayed the correct price to wait for customers.
Since he became the Minister of Justice (司寇, Sīkòu),
the Jì (季), Mèng (孟), and Dōu (郈) families destroyed the walls of Féi (費),
and the people of Qí (齊) returned the territory they had invaded from Lǔ (魯).
This was all brought about by accumulating righteousness.
Therefore, it is said:
"When his person is upright,
he is obeyed without giving orders."
When Sūn Shū'áo (孫叔敖) was an infant,
he went out for a walk
and saw a two-headed snake.
He killed it and buried it,
then returned home and wept.
His mother asked him the reason,
and Shū'áo (叔敖) replied, saying:
"I have heard that whoever sees a two-headed snake will die.
Just now, I saw one.
I am afraid I will leave my mother and die."
His mother said:
"Where is the snake now?"
He said:
"Fearing that others might see it again,
I killed and buried it."
His mother said:
"I have heard that those who have hidden virtue,
Heaven repays with blessings.
You will not die."
When he grew up,
he became the Chancellor of Chǔ (楚).
Even before he governed, the people of the state trusted in his benevolence.
Yǔ (禹) rose to prominence through Túshān (塗山).
Jié's downfall was due to Mòxǐ,
Tāng's rise was due to Yǒushēn,
Zhòu's downfall was due to Dájǐ,
Wén and Wǔ's rise was due to Rènsì,
King Yōu's downfall was due to Bāosì.
Therefore, the *Book of Poetry* rectifies "Guān Jū,"
and the *Spring and Autumn Annals* praises Bójī.
Fán Jī
was the consort of the state of Chǔ.
King Zhuāng of Chǔ dismissed the court and feasted late,
and she asked the reason for it.
King Zhuāng said:
"This morning I spoke with a wise prime minister,
and didn't realize the day was so late."
Fán Jī said:
"Who is this wise prime minister?"
The King said:
"It is Yúqiū Zǐ."
Fán Jī covered her mouth and laughed,
and the king asked the reason for it.
She said:
"I am fortunate to be able to hold the towel and comb to serve the King,
It wasn't that she didn't want exclusive honor and affection,
but she thought it would harm the king's righteousness,
so she recommended several people to the same rank as concubines.
Now, Yúqiū Zǐ has been prime minister for decades,
but has never recommended a single worthy.
To know and not recommend
is disloyal;
to not know
is unwise.
How can he be considered worthy?"
The next morning at court,
the king told Yúqiū Zǐ about Fán Jī's words.
Yúqiū Zǐ bowed his head and said,
"It is as Fán Jī says."
Therefore,
he resigned his position and recommended Sūn Shū'áo.
Sūn Shū'áo became prime minister of Chǔ,
and ultimately King Zhuāng became hegemon,
in which Fán Jī played a part.
During the time of Duke Líng of Wèi,
Qú Bóyù was worthy but not employed,
while Mí Zixiá was unworthy but given responsibilities.
The Wèi grandee Shǐ Qiū worried about this,
and repeatedly advised Duke Líng but was not listened to.
Shǐ Qiū fell ill and was about to die,
and said to his son,
"When I die,
hold the funeral in the north hall.
That I could not promote Qū Bóyù and demote Mí Zǐxiá
means I could not rectify the ruler.
One who in life cannot rectify the ruler
should not have a proper funeral after death.
Placing my corpse in the north hall
will be sufficient for me."
Shǐ Qiū died.
Líng Gōng went to offer condolences.
Seeing the funeral in the north hall,
he asked the reason.
His son explained his father's words to Líng Gōng in detail.
Líng Gōng was startled and changed his expression.
He suddenly realized his error and left his seat,
saying,
"When the master was alive, he wished to promote the worthy and demote the unworthy,
and he did not slacken even in death.
Moreover, he used his corpse to remonstrate.
He can be called loyal and unwavering."
Thereupon,
he summoned Qū Bóyù and promoted him to be a minister.
He demoted Mí Zǐxiá,
moved the funeral to the main hall,
completed the proper rites, and then returned.
The state of Wèi became well-governed.
Shǐ Qiū's courtesy name was Zǐyú.
He is the one referred to in the *Analects* as "How upright is Shǐ Yú!"
The ruler of Jìn asked,
"Who can be appointed as successor?"
Qí Xī replied,
The senior minister of Jìn, Qí Xī, was old.
"Xiè Hú is suitable."
The ruler said,
"Isn't he your enemy?"
He replied,
"Your Majesty asked about suitability,
not about enemies."
Jìn then appointed Xiè Hú.
Later, he asked again,
"Who can be appointed as the national military officer?"
Qí Xī replied,
"Wǔ is suitable."
The ruler said,
"Isn't he your son?"
He replied,
"Your Majesty asked about suitability,
not about my son."
The noble men said that Qí Xī was able to recommend the worthy.
He recommended his enemy
without flattery;
he established his son
without favoritism.
The *Book* says:
“Not partial, not partisan,
the Kingly Way is broad and open.”
This describes Qí Xī.
In external appointments, he did not avoid personal enemies;
in internal appointments, he did not favor relatives.
He can be said to have been supremely impartial.
Because he valued goodness, he could promote those of a similar kind.
The *Book of Odes* says:
“Because he possesses it,
therefore he resembles it.”
Qí Xī possessed this quality.
King Gòng of Chǔ was ill,
and summoned his Prime Minister, saying:
“Cháng Shì Guǎn Sū served me,
he always loyally guided me with principle,
and corrected me with righteousness.
When I am with him,
I am uneasy;
when I don't see him,
I miss him.
However,
I have gained something from him;
his contribution is not small,
I must reward him generously.
Shēn Hóu Bó served me,
he always indulged me.
What I delight in,
he encourages me to do;
what I favor,
he is the first to wear;
when I am with him,
I am happy;
when I don't see him,
I am distressed.
Nevertheless,
I will ultimately gain nothing,
his transgression is not small,
I must quickly send him away."
The *Lìngyǐn* said,
"Yes!"
The next day,
the king died.
The *Lìngyǐn* immediately appointed Guǎnsū as Senior Minister,
and expelled Shēn Hóubó from the borders.
Zēngzǐ said,
"When a bird is about to die,
its cry is mournful;
when a person is about to die,
their words are good."
These words revert to their original nature;
this is what they call Gòng Wáng.
Therefore, Kǒngzǐ said,
"If one hears the Dao in the morning,
one can die in the evening."
How can one hear of posterity,
awaken to the next life?
It is still better than disappearing without ever awakening.
In the past, Wèi Wǔhóu 魏武侯 planned an affair and it was fitting,
none of the assembled officials could match it.
He appeared in court with a happy countenance.
Wú Qǐ 吳起 stepped forward and said,
"Has Your Highness heard something of the words of Chǔ Zhuāngwáng 楚莊王?"
Wǔhóu 武侯 said,
"Not yet.
What were the words of Zhuāngwáng 莊王?"
Wú Qǐ 吳起 said,
"Chǔ Zhuāngwáng 楚莊王 planned an affair and it was fitting,
none of the assembled officials could match it.
He appeared in court with a worried countenance.
Shēn Gōng Wūchén 申公巫臣 stepped forward and said,
'Your Majesty appears in court with a worried countenance,
why is that?'
Zhuāngwáng 莊王 said,
'I have heard that,
of the feudal lords, the one who chooses his own teacher becomes a king,
the one who chooses his own friends becomes a hegemon,
and the one who thinks he is sufficient and none of his officials can match him, will perish.
Now, with my unworthy lack of talent,
when I deliberate in court,
and none of the assembled officials can match my judgment,
"Our state is perhaps on the verge of ruin.
That is why I have a worried expression."
What King Zhuang was worried about,
but you alone have a happy expression,
why is that?"
Marquis Wu hesitated and apologized, saying:
"Heaven has sent you, Master, to correct my faults,
Heaven has sent you, Master, to correct my faults!"
The state of Wei banished Duke Xian.
Duke Dao of Jin said to Shi Kuang:
"The people of Wei expelled their ruler,
is that not excessive?"
He replied:
"Perhaps their ruler was indeed excessive.
For Heaven gives birth to the people and establishes a ruler for them,
to have him oversee and shepherd them,
and not let them lose their nature.
A good ruler will reward good and remove the people's troubles,
love the people like his own children,
cover them like Heaven,
and contain them like Earth.
The people support their ruler,
love him like their parents,
look up to him like the sun and moon,
respect him like the spirits,
and fear him like thunder.
"The ruler,
is the master of the spirits,
and the hope of the people.
Heaven loves the people deeply;
how could it allow one person to be unrestrained above the people,
indulging in their lusts,
and abandoning the nature of Heaven and Earth?
It surely would not.
If you oppress the people's nature,
diminish the sacrifices to the spirits,
the common people will lose hope,
and the state will be without a master,
what use will it be then!
What is the point of not removing him?"
The Duke said:
"Good!"
When Zhào Jiǎnzi ascended the Yángcháng slope,
all the ministers bared their shoulders and pushed the chariot,
but Hǔ Huì alone carried his halberd, walked and sang, and did not push the chariot.
Jiǎnzi said:
"I am ascending the slope,
all the ministers are pushing the chariot,
but Huì alone carries his halberd, walks and sings, and does not push the chariot.
This means that Huì, as a minister, is insulting his lord.
As a minister insulting his lord,
what is his crime?"
Hǔ Huì replied,
"Those who, as ministers, insult their ruler
deserve to die and die again."
Jiǎn Zǐ said,
"What does it mean to 'die and die again'?"
Hǔ Huì said,
"Their body dies,
and their wife and children also die.
This is what is meant by 'die and die again.'
You have already heard the crime of a minister who insults his ruler;
have you also heard of a ruler who insults his ministers?"
Jiǎn Zǐ said,
"What is it like for a ruler to insult his ministers?"
Hǔ Huì replied,
"For a ruler to insult his ministers means
the wise will not offer counsel,
the eloquent will not be sent as envoys,
and the brave will not fight.
If the wise do not offer counsel,
then the state is endangered;
if the eloquent are not sent as envoys,
then diplomatic missions will fail;
if the brave do not fight,
then the borders will be invaded."
Jiǎn Zǐ said,
"Good!"
Thereupon he dismissed the assembled ministers,
and did not have his carriage pushed;
He prepared wine for the scholar-officials,
and drank with the assembled ministers,
giving Hǔ Huì the seat of honor.
1.10 Formerly, Zhōu Shě served Zhào Jiǎnzǐ,
Formerly, Zhōu Shě served Zhào Jiǎn Zǐ.
standing at Zhào Jiǎnzǐ's gate
for three days and three nights.
Jiǎnzǐ sent someone out to ask him, saying:
"What is it, sir, that you would instruct me with?"
Zhōu Shě said:
"I wish to be an outspoken minister,
holding a brush and tablet,
following behind you, my lord,
recording your transgressions and writing them down,
so that there are records daily,
results monthly,
and gains yearly."
Jiǎnzǐ was pleased with this
and kept him nearby.
Before long, Zhōu Shě died,
and Jiǎnzǐ gave him a grand burial.
Three years later,
he was drinking merrily with the various grandees,
when Jiǎnzǐ wept.
The grandees rose and went out, saying:
"We, your servants, have committed a capital crime,
without even knowing it."
Jiǎn Zǐ said:
"Grand Masters rebel,
though without guilt.
Formerly, my friend Zhōu Shě had a saying:
'The hides of a hundred sheep
are not as valuable as the fur under one fox's armpit;
the 'yes-yes' of the multitude
is not as good as Zhōu Shě's outspokenness.
Formerly, Zhòu was muddle-headed and perished,
while Wǔ Wáng was outspoken and prospered.'
Since Zhōu Shě's death,
I have never heard of my faults.
Therefore, if a ruler does not hear his errors or hears them but does not correct them, he will perish.
My state is nearly doomed,
and that is why I weep."
Wèi Wén Hóu was sitting with his officers,
and asked,
"What kind of ruler am I?"
The courtiers all said,
"You,
are a benevolent ruler."
When it came to Dí Huáng,
he said,
"You,
are not a benevolent ruler."
Wèi Wén Hóu said,
"How do you explain this?"
He replied:
"When you attacked Zhōngshān 中山,
you did not use the fief to enfeoff your younger brother,
but used it to enfeoff your eldest son.
From this, I know that you are not a benevolent ruler."
Wén Hóu 文侯 became angry and banished Dí Huáng 翟黃.
Huáng 黃 got up and left.
Next was Rèn Zuò 任座.
Wén Hóu 文侯 asked:
"What kind of ruler am I?"
Rèn Zuò 任座 replied:
"You
are a benevolent ruler."
He said:
"How do you explain this?"
He replied:
"I have heard that
when the ruler is benevolent, his ministers are upright.
Just now, Dí Huáng's 翟黃 words were upright.
From this, I know that you
are a benevolent ruler."
Wén Hóu 文侯 said:
"Good!"
He recalled Dí Huáng 翟黃,
and appointed him as Senior Minister.
Zhōngháng Yín 中行寅 was about to die,
so he summoned his chief priest and wanted to accuse him of a crime.
He said:
"You perform sacrifices for me,
are the sacrificial animals not plump and rich?
Furthermore, are your purifications and abstinences not reverent?
What is the reason for the downfall of my state?"
The priest Jiǎn 簡 replied:
"In the past, my former lord, Zhōngháng Mùzǐ 中行穆子,
had only ten leather chariots,
and he did not worry about their inadequacy,
but worried about the inadequacy of virtue and righteousness.
Now, my lord, you have a hundred armored chariots,
and you do not worry about the inadequacy of virtue and righteousness,
but only worry about the inadequacy of chariots.
When boats and chariots are ornamented,
then taxes and levies are heavy;
when taxes and levies are heavy, then the people resent and curse.
Moreover, if you truly believe that prayers are beneficial to the state,
then curses will also cause harm,
generation after generation, the state will perish.
One person prays for it,
and the whole country curses it;
one prayer cannot overcome ten thousand curses,
and the state perishes,
is that not fitting?
What crime has the priest committed?"
Zhōngháng Zǐ 中行子 was then ashamed.
When Qín 秦 desired to attack Chǔ 楚,
they sent an envoy to observe the treasures of Chǔ 楚.
The King of Chǔ 楚 heard of this
and summoned the Chancellor Zǐ Xī 子西 and asked him,
saying:
"Qín 秦 desires to observe the treasures of Chǔ 楚.
Our Hé Shì Zhī Bì 和氏之璧 jade,
the Zhū of Suí Hóu 隨侯之珠,
can we show them these?"
The Chancellor Zǐ Xī 子西 answered,
"I do not know."
He summoned Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 and asked him.
Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 answered,
"This is to observe the gains and losses of our state and to plan against it.
It is not about the treasures;
it is about the worthy ministers.
Pearls, jades, and playthings
are not the most precious things."
The king then sent Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 to respond to them.
Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 dispatched three hundred elite soldiers
and arrayed them inside the Western Gate.
He prepared one altar facing east,
four altars facing south,
and one altar facing west.
When the envoy of Qín 秦 arrived,
Zhāo Xīxù 昭奚恤 said:
"Jūn,
you are a guest,
please take the superior seat facing east."
The Chief Minister Zǐxī faced south,
Grand Clan Elder Zǐ'áo was next in order,
Lord Yè Zǐgāo was next in order,
the Minister of War Zǐfǎn was next in order.
Zhāo Xīxù took his place on the western side of the altar,
and said:
"The guest wishes to see the treasures of the state of Chǔ,
what the state of Chǔ treasures are its virtuous ministers.
To govern the people,
to fill the granaries,
and to enable the people to obtain what they need,
the Chief Minister Zǐxī is here;
to present jade tablets,
to envoy to the feudal lords,
to resolve the difficulty of resentments,
to cultivate joy between the two states,
to ensure there are no worries of war,
Grand Clan Elder Zǐ'áo is here;
to guard the borders,
to be cautious of the boundaries,
not to invade neighboring countries,
and neighboring countries also do not suffer invasion,
Lord Yè Zǐgāo is here;
to manage the armies,
to prepare the weapons,
To face a powerful enemy,
to raise the drumstick and beat the drum,
to mobilize a million troops,
to command all to rush into boiling water and fire,
to tread upon gleaming blades,
to emerge from difficulties where ten thousand deaths are risked for a single chance of survival—
Sīmǎ Zǐfǎn is here for this;
harboring the remaining plans of a hegemon king,
managing the remaining customs of governing amidst chaos,
Zhāo Xīxù is here for this.
They are the object of attention for great states."
The Qin envoy, alarmed, had nothing to say in response.
Zhāo Xīxù then bowed and departed.
The Qin envoy returned,
and said to the Qin ruler:
"Chǔ has many capable ministers,
it is not yet advisable to attack them."
Consequently, they did not attack Chǔ.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"A multitude of accomplished scholars,
King Wén was made tranquil by them."
This is what it means.
Duke Píng of Jìn desired to attack Qí and
sent Fàn Zhāo to observe them.
Duke Jǐng gave him wine as a gift.
In his cups,
Fàn Zhāo said:
"I would like to request a drink from your wine vessel, my lord."
The Duke said:
"Pour from my vessel,
and offer it to the guest."
Fàn Zhāo finished his drink.
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Remove the vessel,
and change it!"
The wine vessel and cup were prepared.
Fàn Zhāo feigned drunkenness and, displeased, arose to dance,
and said to the Grand Music Master:
"Can you perform the music of Chéngzhōu for me?
I will dance it for you."
The Grand Music Master said:
"Your humble servant is not familiar with it."
Fàn Zhāo quickly left.
Duke Jǐng said to Yàn Zǐ:
"Jìn
is a great state.
When they send envoys,
they will observe our government.
Now you have angered the envoy of a great state,
what will we do?"
Yàn Zǐ said:
"This Fàn Zhāo,
is not ignorant and unacquainted with propriety.
He merely wishes to test our ruler and ministers,
gù jué zhī yě." Therefore, he severed relations with him.
Jǐng Gōng wèi tàishī yuē: "
Zǐ hé yǐ bù wèi kè tiáo Chéngzhōu zhī yuè hū?" Duke Jing said to the Grand Music Master: "Why don't you tune the music of Cheng Zhou for the guest?"
Tàishī duì yuē: "
Fū Chéngzhōu zhī yuè,
tiānzǐ zhī yuè yě,
ruò tiáo zhī,
bì rén zhǔ wǔ zhī.
Jīn Fàn Zhāo rén chén yě,
ér yù wǔ tiānzǐ zhī yuè,

chén gù bù wéi yě." The Grand Music Master replied: "The music of Cheng Zhou is the music of the Son of Heaven. If I were to tune it, it would certainly be the ruler of men who would dance to it. Now, Fàn Zhāo is a subject, and he wishes to dance to the music of the Son of Heaven; therefore, I will not do it."
Fàn Zhāo guī,
yǐ gào Píng Gōng yuē:
"Qí wèi kě fá yě,
chén yù shì qí jūn,
ér Yàn Zǐ shí zhī;
chén yù fàn qí lǐ,

ér tàishī zhī zhī." Fàn Zhāo returned and reported to Duke Ping, saying, "Qi is not yet ready to be attacked. I wanted to test their ruler, and Yàn Zǐ recognized it; I wanted to violate their propriety, and the Grand Music Master knew it."
Zhòngní wén zhī yuē:
"Fū bù chū yú zūn zǔ zhī jiān,
ér zhī qiānlǐ zhī wài,
qí Yàn Zǐ zhī wèi yě,
kěwèi zhéchōng yǐ,

ér tàishī qí yǔ yān." Confucius heard of this and said, "Indeed, without leaving the wine cups and stands, he knows what is happening a thousand miles away. That is what Yàn Zǐ is like. He can be said to ward off attacks, and the Grand Music Master is involved in this as well."
Jìn Píng Gōng fú Xī Hé,
zhōng liú ér tàn yuē:
"Alas!
Where can I find worthy scholars to share this joy with?"
The boatman, Gù Sāng, replied,
"Your words are excessive.
For swords are produced in Yuè,
pearls are produced in the Jiāng and Hàn rivers,
jade is produced on Mount Kūn,
these three treasures,
all arrive without feet.
Now, if you truly cherish scholars,
then worthy scholars will arrive!"
Píng Gōng said,
"Gù Sāng, come here!
I have more than three thousand retainers under my gate.
If morning provisions are insufficient,
I collect market taxes in the evening;
if evening provisions are insufficient,
I collect market taxes in the morning.
Can I still be said to not cherish scholars?"
Gù Sāng replied,
"Now, the swan flies high, soaring into the sky,
but what it relies on is only its six wing feathers.
As for the down on its belly
and the fur on its back,
whether you add or remove a handful,
its flight will not be affected.
I wonder, of your three thousand retainers, are they wing feathers,
or are they down and fur?"
Píng Gōng remained silent and did not respond.
Chǔ Wēi Wáng asked Sòng Yù,
"Does the Master perhaps have some unusual conduct?
Why is it that the scholars and common people do not praise him very much?"
Sòng Yù replied,
"Yes,
indeed,
there is.
I hope that Your Majesty will pardon my offense
and allow me to finish my explanation.
There was a guest who sang in Yǐng zhōng.
At first, he sang 'Xiàlǐ Bārén' (Lowland Commoner),
and those in the capital who joined in and harmonized numbered in the thousands.
When he sang 'Yánglíng Cǎiwēi' (Gathering Ferns on Yánglíng),
those in the capital who joined in and harmonized numbered in the hundreds.
When he sang 'Yángchūn Báixuě' (Sunshine and White Snow),
those in the capital who joined in and harmonized numbered only in the tens.
When he drew out the shāng notes, carved the jiǎo notes,
and mixed in flowing zhǐ notes,
those in the capital who joined in and harmonized
were no more than a few.
It is the case that the higher the tune,
the fewer harmonize with it.
Thus, among birds there is the phoenix, and among fish there is the whale.
The phoenix soars upward to nine thousand miles,
piercing through the floating clouds,
Bearing the azure sky on its back,
soaring above the deep darkness.
How can the quail of the dung-heap field,
possibly fathom the height of heaven and earth with it?

Duke Píng of Jìn was dwelling in leisure,

inferior talents occupy high positions,

When laws are not enforced,
officials and the people are not upright,

My blackness,
